01 / Repetition & restraint

What happens on the third “Hmm”?

Compare two or three nearby cue opportunities. This isolated comparison starts with an empty history; the conversation’s recent-use history persists across turns.

Before · one repeated cue

    After · vary, then give space

      90 seconds before the same take returns. Avoid the last two cue families. At most two voiced cues per 20 seconds; another opportunity gets a gesture and silence.

      Proposed listening-test defaults, not measured fatigue thresholds. If a ready local cue is missing or ineligible, remain silent.

      Recent conversation choices · silent simulation

      • No cues used yet
      See the semantic, prosodic and gesture palette
      Receipt

      Soft level-to-falling hum, quiet breath, or “One moment.” Brief glance to the person; no claim of understanding.

      Interruption

      Settled low grunt, short closed “Mm,” or “Go ahead.” Stop the old gesture and face the person.

      Post-inference

      Gentle intake, low assent, or “Let’s start there.” Requires received text that makes the bridge eligible.

      Continuation

      Soft reflective exhale, low resonant hum, or “Staying with that thought…” Only after the relevant completed unit; peer into the ball, then look back.
